categories.name: New benchmark exposes a hidden failure
categories.definition: The paper builds a more realistic, composite or interactive evaluation and shows that models that look strong on existing benchmarks fail badly. A remedy is optional.
categories.include_if: The main artifact is a benchmark or test protocol, and the headline finding is that current state-of-the-art systems perform much worse or differently than standard scores suggest.
categories.exclude_if: The benchmark serves a domain that has no evaluation at all and the story is about enabling work there, not about overturning what looked like competence (use resource-for-underserved-domain). It is also excluded when the benchmark is a side component of a newly defined threat or task (use new-problem-or-threat).

categories.name: Resource unlocks an underserved domain
categories.definition: The paper supplies a dataset, data-generation pipeline or expert-grounded evaluation for a domain where data or evaluation was missing, and shows that training or evaluating on it changes what is achievable.
categories.include_if: The main contribution is a dataset or data framework, and the payoff is new capability, better generalization or the first reliable measurement in a specific domain.
categories.exclude_if: The point is that existing top models break, not that the domain becomes possible to work on (use benchmark-exposes-gap).

categories.name: Name a new problem or threat
categories.definition: The paper formalizes a problem, attack surface or pipeline step that prior work never posed, shows it matters in practice, and provides first measurements or baselines.
categories.include_if: Before this paper the question was not asked at all (e.g., detecting unlearned models, cross-user poisoning, forget-set curation), and a task formulation is central.
categories.exclude_if: The task is already known and the paper only measures it more realistically (use benchmark-exposes-gap). The paper is also excluded when it relaxes an assumption of an existing problem to get guarantees (use provable-reach-extended).

categories.name: Diagnose the root cause, then fix it
categories.definition: Starting from a known shortfall, an analysis pinpoints a specific mechanistic cause, and a targeted method that removes that cause recovers the lost performance.
categories.include_if: The paper has an explicit two-act structure: analysis names a culprit (credit misassignment, lazy reflection, spectral mismatch), then a method is designed against that culprit.
categories.exclude_if: The analysis is a formal theory that defines the right quantity to optimize, rather than an empirical diagnosis of a failure (use principled-replacement). The paper is also excluded when the fix is mainly a way to get both sides of a trade-off and the diagnosis is minor (use tradeoff-dissolved).

categories.name: Get both sides of an assumed trade-off
categories.definition: The field believes you must pick between two goods (speed vs. stability, fairness vs. truthfulness, flexibility vs. cost), and the paper's method achieves both.
categories.include_if: The 'seems' side states an explicit dichotomy or tension, and the 'really' side shows a design that keeps both properties.
categories.exclude_if: The belief is only that one component is required, with no second good at stake (use unnecessary-component). The paper is also excluded when the gain is reaching a scale or bound regime through structural assumptions (use provable-reach-extended).

categories.name: The 'necessary' ingredient isn't
categories.definition: A component the field treats as required (a vision latent, graph priors, NMS, score conversion, a large LLM, anchors, many sequential rounds) is shown to be dispensable, and a simpler or cheaper pipeline matches or beats the standard one.
categories.include_if: The headline claim is 'you don't need X', and the method demonstrates this by removing or replacing X.
categories.exclude_if: Removing X is presented as getting both sides of a stated trade-off (use tradeoff-dissolved). The paper is also excluded when the main payoff is explaining why X seemed to work (use mechanism-revealed).

categories.name: Reveal what actually drives the behaviour
categories.definition: Analysis uncovers the true mechanism behind an observed effect or behaviour (compression, not reasoning; alignment, not missing structure; decode-time, not prefill, subspaces). The finding is then often exploited cheaply.
categories.include_if: The core contribution is an explanatory or causal account of an existing model or phenomenon, and any method is a direct consequence of that account.
categories.exclude_if: The account is a formal theorem about rates or optimal quantities (use theory-overturns-intuition). The paper is also excluded when the analysis exists only to motivate fixing a specific failure (use diagnose-then-fix).

categories.name: Sharper theory overturns an intuition
categories.definition: Rigorous analysis shows that a presumed rate, relation or sufficient condition is wrong: costs add rather than multiply, acceleration can hurt, KL-closeness does not imply similar representations, only covariance matters.
categories.include_if: The 'really' side is a theorem or bound contradicting a natural belief, and any algorithm mainly serves to realize or illustrate that bound.
categories.exclude_if: The theory is used to design a replacement for a heuristic, and the method is the headline (use principled-replacement). The paper is also excluded when the result is mainly reaching a new scale or setting (use provable-reach-extended).

categories.name: Rigorous comparison overturns folk wisdom
categories.definition: Large, carefully controlled experiments or a predictive-fit methodology show that a widely held empirical ranking or recipe judgement is an artifact of unfair or small-scale comparison.
categories.include_if: The main contribution is an experimental methodology (strict parity, scaling fits, large ablation sweeps) whose results reverse a conventional conclusion.
categories.exclude_if: A new benchmark or task is the artifact (use benchmark-exposes-gap). The reversal is also excluded when it is proved rather than measured (use theory-overturns-intuition).

categories.name: Principled theory replaces a heuristic
categories.definition: The paper shows that a heuristic practice is suboptimal or unanalyzed and replaces it with a method derived from theory (information theory, extreme-value tails, geometry), backed by guarantees.
categories.include_if: The pitch is 'heuristic → principled with guarantees': the heuristic is shown to be biased or unexplained, and the new method comes with theorems.
categories.exclude_if: The theorem itself, not the method, is the headline (use theory-overturns-intuition). The paper is also excluded when the motivation is an empirical diagnosis of a failure (use diagnose-then-fix).

categories.name: Extend guarantees or scale to a harder regime
categories.definition: Results previously limited to small, exact-access or whole-stream settings are carried to million-node graphs, time-decay streams, black-box lower levels or polylogarithmic memory. This is usually done by exploiting structure or weaker assumptions.
categories.include_if: The 'seems' side is 'infeasible, or only known under assumption A', and the 'really' side is a provable algorithm that works in the harder regime.
categories.exclude_if: Two competing goods are both obtained, with no regime change (use tradeoff-dissolved). The paper is also excluded when the result says an existing rate or intuition is wrong (use theory-overturns-intuition).

categories.name: Decompose what was treated as one thing
categories.definition: A signal, state or attribution treated as a single object is split into components (line-level rewards, spatial vs. memory contributions, action-responsive vs. exogenous state), and modelling each separately fixes the problem.
categories.include_if: The key move is a decomposition, and the method directly operates on the parts.
categories.exclude_if: The decomposition only diagnoses a failure that a different mechanism then fixes (use diagnose-then-fix). The paper is also excluded when the split serves a benchmark's failure analysis (use benchmark-exposes-gap).

categories.name: Unify scattered methods as one family
categories.definition: Methods seen as separate are shown to be instances or approximations of one framework, which explains them and yields new variants, libraries or design freedom.
categories.include_if: The 'seems' side is 'A and B are different', and the 'really' side is a common derivation or framework within the same field.
categories.exclude_if: The unifying lens is imported from a different discipline, and the problem is recast as that field's problem (use cross-field-reframe).

categories.name: Recast the problem in another field's terms
categories.definition: The paper argues that an ML problem is really an instance of a mature problem from another area (probabilistic programming, systems security, KV-cache reconciliation) and imports that area's abstractions to solve it.
categories.include_if: The pitch is 'X is really a Y problem', and the contribution is the formulation plus a system or principles imported from Y.
categories.exclude_if: Methods within the same field are merged, with no import from another discipline (use unification).

unused_or_rare: niche:new-problem (2 uses: 3274, 8717; 1707 and 7079 also fit but got overlooked-aspect or underexplored-setting)
contribution:negative-result (3 uses, but 3769, 7228 and 7781 are also essentially negative results)
arc:local-is-general (5 uses, applied inconsistently: 1214 is a reframing and 3264 is generalization from data, not 'local is general')
niche:new-setting-transfer (4 uses, which overlap with underexplored-setting)
overlapping_pairs: Co-assigned on 2454, 1993, 2935, 6088, 7100 and 8871. Any trade-off can be phrased as 'giving up B seemed necessary', so annotators cannot separate the two.
Co-assigned on 0731, 3678, 3973, 4173 and 0180. 'You cannot have both' and 'infeasible' describe the same story.
Both describe structure the field missed. 3206 has both labels plus different-are-same.
Both mean 'prior work did not look here'. The choice between them looks arbitrary (e.g., 1707 vs 7079).
Usually both are true. They are co-assigned on 2454 and 4173, and the choice is driven by wording.
Nearly every benchmark paper gets both (5220, 7228, 7781, 3178, 4301).
missing: An arc for 'new benchmark exposes the gap'. v0 forces benchmark papers into better-on-axis (7228 has only better-on-axis) or seems-to-work-doesnt.
An arc for diagnose-then-fix, i.e., a two-act structure where analysis motivates the method (4047, 5949, 6088).
Cross-field reframing ('X is really a Y problem': 0342, 1214, 8602).
A rigorous controlled comparison or methodology arc (1322, 4363).
An explain-then-exploit sequence (2955, 1185), as distinct from a bare hidden-relation.
A contribution type for position or SoK papers (1214 is shoehorned into task-formulation and characterization).
axis_problems: overlooked-aspect is assigned to about 25 of 60 papers, so it barely discriminates and works as a default niche label.
seems-necessary-isnt (~21/60) and seems-to-work-doesnt (~19/60) together cover most papers. They are frames for the seems→really sentence that every paper has, so they are not distinct story types.
method appears in about 48/60 contribution lists, which makes the contribution axis almost uninformative unless the primary contribution is marked.
better-on-axis is used as filler for dataset and benchmark papers (5220, 7228, 3178) whose story is not an improvement on an axis.
The arc labels mix belief-content patterns (seems-necessary-isnt) with structural patterns (one-is-several, different-are-same). They are not one axis, so double-labelling is constant.

notes: The parent fields name four families (evaluation-led, belief-overturn, method-led, reframing). They are not separate entries, and they let a pitch be chosen coarse-to-fine. Assign one primary archetype by asking what the abstract's first claim is: benchmark, 'you don't need X', 'get both', a theorem, and so on. Mark secondary archetypes separately, because many papers chain two (e.g., 4301 is benchmark-exposes-gap then a fix; 2955 is mechanism-revealed then a method). The hardest boundaries are unnecessary-component vs tradeoff-dissolved and theory-overturns-intuition vs principled-replacement. Resolve them by whether a second good is explicitly at stake, and by whether the theorem or the method is the headline. controlled-comparison-overturns, decompose-the-monolith and cross-field-reframe are small here (2-3 items) but are distinct, transferable pitches. A larger sample should check whether they stay separate or should be merged into their families. v0 should be refactored into one primary-arc label plus orthogonal flags (primary contribution type, has-theory, has-benchmark) instead of free multi-labels.
